glossdef.p: The graphics processing unit is a dedicated processor, separate from the CPU, that draws images and graphics. The power of your GPU will determine how good displayed images look. This is likely the most or second most expensive part in your computer if you want to play games or do any kind of video editing or modeling.

GPUs are good at doing large numbers of repetitive tasks, such as drawing hundreds of image frames per second with only slight differences. This also makes GPUs decent at cryptography and generative AI application, although not as good as a specially designed dedicated component. But because GPUs are good enough at those tasks they can be subject to high price volatility whenever a new technology takes off. More than any other component price and availability for GPUs can vary wildly.
There are two major GPU competitors, Nvidia and AMD. As a general rule Nvidia pushes performance with a price tag to match while AMD offers more budget conscious GPUs.
